author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
CI has been generating API documentation without ever building the packages it documents, so every cross-package type reference silently resolved wrong.

`docs/src/content/docs/api/theme/src.md` documents:

```
> **mergeThemes**(`baseTheme`, `overrideTheme`): `ThemeConfig`
```

The source says otherwise — `packages/theme/src/utils/token-transformer.ts:276`:

```ts
mergeThemes(baseTheme: ThemeConfig, overrideTheme: Partial<ThemeConfig>): ThemeConfig
```

`Partial<ThemeConfig>`, not `ThemeConfig`. There is one `mergeThemes` in the package, so this is not a mis-documented overload.

## The mechanism

Three things line up:

1. `.github/actions/setup-ci` ends at `pnpm install`. It never builds.
2. Every `@sparkle/*` package resolves only through `dist` — `@sparkle/types` exports `{".": {"types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js"}}` — and `dist` is gitignored, so it does not exist on a fresh checkout.
3. `docs/typedoc.json` sets `skipErrorChecking: true`.

TypeDoc runs with `entryPointStrategy: resolve` against package **sources**, so `packages/theme/src` parses fine. But resolving `ThemeConfig`, which `@sparkle/theme` imports from `@sparkle/types`, goes through that `exports` map into a `dist` that is not there.

`skipErrorChecking` means that failure is not raised. TypeDoc mis-resolves the reference and keeps going, and `Partial<ThemeConfig>` renders as bare `ThemeConfig`. The docs are wrong and nothing is red.

Locally the same command is correct, because a local tree almost always has `dist` present from a previous build. That is why this survived: it only reproduces on a clean checkout, which is exactly what CI does every time and a developer almost never does.

## Isolated to one variable

Both runs invoke `typedoc --options typedoc.json` directly, not through the automation wrapper, so the pipeline is not part of the result: [description truncated to fit budget]
title: fix(ci): build packages before TypeDoc so cross-package types resolve
